gaps.sentence: Please ___ me to post this letter.
gaps.hint: make somebody not forget: ___ somebody to do something
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody to do something' means to make someone remember; 'remember' is something you do yourself.

gaps.sentence: Unemployment has ___ sharply since the spring.
gaps.explanation: 'Has risen' — rise does not take an object.

gaps.sentence: Pens, envelopes and paper are sold in the ___ department.
gaps.explanation: 'Stationery' means writing materials; 'stationary' is an adjective meaning not moving.

gaps.sentence: Smoke could be seen ___ from the factory chimneys.
gaps.hint: the smoke goes up by itself — no object
gaps.explanation: 'Rise' (no object) describes the smoke going up; 'raise' would need an object (raise something).

gaps.sentence: Our team has a good ___ of winning on Saturday.
gaps.hint: pattern: have a good ___ of doing something
gaps.explanation: 'Have a chance of doing something' is the standard collocation for the likelihood of success.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her excellent presentation.
gaps.explanation: 'Compliment somebody on something' means to praise; 'complement' means to go well with.

gaps.sentence: ___ at this old photo — isn't it amazing?
gaps.explanation: 'Look at' means to direct your eyes towards something; the other verbs cannot be followed by 'at' here.

gaps.sentence: Thousands of people were forced to ___ their homes.
gaps.hint: a verb is needed after 'to'; meaning: abandon
gaps.explanation: 'Desert' is also a verb meaning to abandon; 'dessert' is only the sweet course of a meal.
